scope: Research audit only; no production data or implementation edited by this agent.
conclusions: The missing relation needs quantitative reduction recipes rather than equal-ratio instance-specialization flags.
On connected unweighted inputs, an alpha-approximate connected dominating set is a 3alpha-approximate ordinary dominating set in the same rounds.
The four-round LOCAL connector has a directly checked conservative multiplier 1+2d when all depth-one minors have edge density at most d.
The published 2d size lemma has a path counterexample; this alone does not refute the published 2dalpha approximation theorem, whose benchmark is the connected optimum.

cwy.title: Caro, West and Yuster, Connected Domination and Spanning Trees with Many Leaves
cwy.verified: For connected G and dominating X with t induced components, gamma_c(G) <= |X|+2t-2. Consequently gamma <= gamma_c <= 3gamma-2.

dkm2019.title: Deurer, Kuhn and Maus, Deterministic Distributed Dominating Set Approximation in the CONGEST Model
dkm2019.location: Section 4, Claim 4.1 and algorithm outline; Theorem 1.4
dkm2019.verified: The distance-three auxiliary graph on a dominating set is connected exactly when the original graph is. A spanning tree yields size below 3|D| but diameter-dependent rounds. A deterministic sparse-skeleton construction gives O(|D|) output with subpolynomial, rather than constant, CONGEST overhead.

gha2014.title: Ghaffari, Near-Optimal Distributed Approximation of Minimum-Weight Connected Dominating Set
gha2014.verified: Weighted connected domination has global dependence. The unweighted case admits polylogarithmic CONGEST approximation by combining domination with a sparse skeleton; this does not justify a four-round CONGEST connector.

recipes.name: Forget the connectivity constraint
recipes.proof: The returned set is feasible for domination; |C| <= alpha gamma_c <= alpha(3gamma-2) <= 3alpha gamma.
restrictions: Source model, randomness, IDs, preprocessing and initial knowledge are retained without extra requirements
Use integral connected OPT; no fractional-domination benchmark is inferred.

recipes.name: Connect a dominating set through depth-one clusters
proofSteps: In three LOCAL rounds learn radius-three neighborhoods, including seed-membership flags and unique IDs.
Assign each vertex to its nearest seed, breaking ties consistently by IDs. Radius-one clusters contract to a connected depth-one minor H with |D| vertices.
Choose one canonical center-to-center path of length at most three for every H-edge. In one further round its endpoints notify the internal vertices.
Retain D and all notified vertices. The output is connected and dominating, with size at most |D|+2|E(H)| <= (1+2d)|D|.
restrictions: Nonempty connected graph and unweighted seed output
LOCAL with unique IDs; no four-round CONGEST or anonymous claim
d is any nonnegative valid depth-one minor edge-density bound and need not be known initially
Singletons work without a special density floor
Seed fractional-domination guarantees may be weakened to integral connected OPT; preserve the original benchmark only as source provenance.
recipes.classification: Independently counted conservative consequence of the cited construction, not the source-stated 2d multiplier.

sizeLemmaIssue.preciseScope: The counterexample below refutes the source-stated size bound. It does not by itself refute its approximation theorem, because OPT_CDS can be larger than OPT_DS.

counterexample.reason: Every connected dominating set on a path contains all internal vertices 2 through 8.

sizeLemmaIssue.proofGap: A path with at most 2r+1 edges can have 2r internal vertices. The source proof counts at most 2r-1. Its 2d size claim is therefore not established by the presented counting argument.
sizeLemmaIssue.forestApproximationNuance: Although 2|D| can fail as a size bound, a 2alpha approximation relative to connected OPT can have a separate proof on forests: the hull of D contains the mandatory internal vertices and adds at most |D| selected leaves. Do not conflate this with the false size inequality.
sizeLemmaIssue.recommendation: Use the independently checked 1+2d recipe until an applicable corrected proof or author clarification supports a stronger multiplier; keep published source claims distinct.

disconnectedInputs: A globally connected dominating set is infeasible on a disconnected nonempty graph with multiple components. Componentwise CDS is a different output convention. Applying a connected-input algorithm componentwise also requires checking its global-parameter inputs, so the reduction must retain connected input explicitly.
lowerBoundCaution: The boolean same-factor problem-inclusion engine must not directly inherit these quantitative transfers. CDS alpha in T implies DS 3alpha in T; the reverse conservative recipe changes both factor and rounds. Any lower-bound conversion must invert these losses and retain all graph/model/domain restrictions.
